# Phase 0 R4 — Clean Domain and Schema Design

Date: 2026-09-09. Scope: DESIGN ONLY. All future model choices below are **RECOMMENDATIONS**, not implemented behavior or approved KNEC policy.

## 1. Governing evidence and boundaries

Read governing sources: [copilot-instructions.md](copilot-instructions.md), [DEVELOPMENT_RULES.md](DEVELOPMENT_RULES.md), [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md), [SECURITY_REQUIREMENTS.md](SECURITY_REQUIREMENTS.md), [ASSESSMENT_SPECIFICATION.md](ASSESSMENT_SPECIFICATION.md), [TESTING_STANDARDS.md](TESTING_STANDARDS.md), [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), [FRESH_DATABASE_REBUILD_PLAN.md](FRESH_DATABASE_REBUILD_PLAN.md), and [PHASE_0R3_FRESH_TARGET_EVIDENCE.md](PHASE_0R3_FRESH_TARGET_EVIDENCE.md).

**FACT:** Inspected `lib/db/schema.ts`, `lib/db/index.ts`, `lib/auth.ts`, `lib/r2.ts`, `lib/activity.ts`, the six `app/actions/` modules, auth and media download routes, package scripts, migration SQL and journal. The source declares **11** public tables: four auth and seven application tables. Earlier documents saying 12 or eight application tables have inconsistent counts. No new database inspection was performed for R4.

**FACT from R3 evidence:** Owner-reported target is project `broad-field-23876929`, branch `schoolhub-fresh-dev`, database `neondb`; PostgreSQL 17.11 and zero rows were verified. This means **empty tables, not an absent public schema**: R3 lists 11 existing public tables and nine empty `neon_auth` tables. Provider branch ID/project association remains owner-reported. A future initial migration cannot assume no tables exist. Resolve bootstrap treatment before execution; R4 does not reset or baseline anything.

**FACT:** Better Auth uses the shared `pg` pool; the four public auth tables have their own identity contract. `neon_auth` is a separate ownership boundary, not a substitute identity source. Only session/account relationships currently declare FKs. Existing portfolio and file paths have inadequate object scope; notices/calendar are generally user-scoped. Authentication, folders, staff resources, media including bulk upload/download, learner portfolios, notices, calendar and activity/dashboard views must eventually survive as secured capabilities.

**REQUIREMENT:** No schema/source/auth/R2/environment changes, migration generation/execution, SQL mutation, UI redesign or code deletion in R4. This document is the only artifact. Preserve existing unrelated worktree changes. The old schema comment discouraging FKs is superseded for this proposal by the user's explicit integrity requirement; source remains unchanged.

## 2. Model conventions — part of every table contract

The catalogue below plus these defaults fully specifies each proposed application table. `?` means nullable; every other listed column is NOT NULL. IDs are UUIDs except Better Auth IDs, which remain text. Codes, names, statuses and descriptors are bounded text; counts/ordinals are integers; marks and fractions use exact `numeric(18,8)`, never floating point; sizes are bigint; booleans are explicit. `jsonb` is restricted to versioned configuration payloads, diagnostic metadata and immutable snapshots, never a replacement for relationship FKs.

- **T (tenant scope):** `id` PK; `school_id -> schools.id`; unique `(school_id,id)`. Every FK to another T table includes `school_id` and references its `(school_id,id)` unique key. Every table marked T inherits these columns and constraints. All references below name the target table; omitted target column means `id`.
- **G (global):** `id` PK, no `school_id`; explicitly shared catalogues or platform administration only. Global catalogues are read-only to school roles. Global entries do not grant tenant access.
- **M (mutable lifecycle):** `created_at`, `updated_at` as UTC `timestamptz`; `created_by_actor_id`, `updated_by_actor_id -> audit_actors`; `row_version` bigint > 0; optional `archived_at`. Updates increment row version. Actor-school validity is transaction-checked because actors can also represent platform/services.
- **I (immutable):** `created_at`, `created_by_actor_id -> audit_actors`; no ordinary update/delete. Subsequent facts use new rows. Explicit operational status fields are exceptions only where stated.
- **Keys/indexes:** PKs and all U (unique) declarations get indexes. Add a referencing-side btree for every FK, school-leading for tenant FKs, unless an existing index has those same leading columns. X lists additional access indexes. No blanket indexing of JSON or large text.
- **Deletion/history (D):** Default for every FK is `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, including school and auth references. M records archive/deactivate after use; retain referenced history. An unreferenced erroneous draft can be hard-deleted only through an authorized audited transaction. I records retain history and cannot be routinely deleted. No tenant cascade to scores, evidence or results. Purging requires a separately approved retention process; no retention duration is invented here.
- **Checks (C):** Nonblank required codes/names, positive versions/ordinals, valid enumerated lifecycle values, and ordered start/end dates apply wherever relevant. Cross-row sums, date containment, state transitions and assignment authority are enforced by locked domain transactions and deferred constraint triggers where necessary, not misrepresented as simple SQL CHECKs.
- **Context keys:** Where a child repeats year, grade, class, subject, enrolment or assessment IDs for consistency, parents expose additional unique `(school_id,id,<context columns>)` keys. Composite FKs bind that whole tuple. These redundant keys are integrity supports, not alternate identities. Nullable context has explicit shape checks and NULLS NOT DISTINCT uniqueness where specified.

## 3. Proposed table catalogue

Each entry gives purpose/relationships, columns and FKs, U/X/C and D in addition to its inherited scope and lifecycle contract.

### 3.1 Authentication boundary (existing, retained contract)

These four tables are **not redesigned**; names/camelCase, types, nullability and provider behavior must be compatibility-verified against the installed Better Auth contract before R5. They do not inherit T/M/I defaults.

| Table / purpose | PK, columns, nullability and FKs | Uniques / indexes / checks | Scope, deletion and history |
|---|---|---|---|
| `public.user` / login identity | text `id` PK; required `name,email,emailVerified,createdAt,updatedAt`; optional `image`; timestamps retain current adapter contract | U email; PK/email indexes; no new checks proposed | Global identity; memberships reference it with RESTRICT; deactivate access via membership/session policy. Pseudonymization and account deletion require a reviewed workflow preserving academic actors. |
| `public.session` / sessions | text `id` PK; required `expiresAt,token,createdAt,updatedAt,userId`; optional `ipAddress,userAgent`; `userId -> user` | U token; X userId, expiresAt; no new checks without adapter validation | Global auth-only; existing user FK CASCADE; revoke/expire and purge per auth policy; not academic history. |
| `public.account` / provider credentials | text `id` PK; required `accountId,providerId,userId,createdAt,updatedAt`; optional `accessToken,refreshToken,idToken,accessTokenExpiresAt,refreshTokenExpiresAt,scope,password`; `userId -> user` | PK; X userId; provider/account uniqueness to verify with adapter, not silently add | Global auth-only; existing user FK CASCADE; no credentials in business/audit payloads; retention under auth policy. |
| `public.verification` / verification state | text `id` PK; required `identifier,value,expiresAt`; optional `createdAt,updatedAt` as current source | PK; X identifier, expiresAt; no assumed identifier uniqueness | Global auth-only, no FK; expire/purge under auth policy; no academic retention. |

No proposed FK targets `neon_auth`. All nine provider tables remain outside application migrations. Do not assume server startup will create public auth tables.

Bootstrap service actor is provisioned only in later approved setup. |

Assessor must cover offering and be authorized now. All rubric child marks inserted atomically; no partial committed marking revision. |

| `moderation_decisions` / immutable review of exact score revision | T/I; `score_revision_id -> score_revisions`, `moderator_assignment_id -> moderator_assignments`, `decision` (approved/returned/rejected), `reason,review_round`, `evidence_manifest_hash` | U (school,score_revision,review_round); X (school,moderator_assignment,created_at); C review_round > 0 | Retain. Reviewer actor must differ from score assessor actor even across memberships/roles; assignment must cover assessment. Return creates another score revision, not altered marks. Evidence hash binds reviewed links/versions. |
| `result_snapshots` / immutable calculated outcome at any aggregation level | T/I; `enrolment_id -> learner_enrolments`, `policy_id -> assessment_policies`, `component_id -> policy_components`, `kind` (task/assessment/subject_term/subject_year/term_total/year_total/cumulative), `task_id? -> assessment_tasks`, `assessment_id? -> assessments`, `school_subject_id? -> school_subjects`, `term_id? -> terms`, `revision,supersedes_id? -> result_snapshots`, `numerator,denominator,normalized_value?,outcome` (scored/absent/exempt/incomplete), `engine_version,rounding_rule,input_hash,context_snapshot` jsonb | U (school,enrolment,component,kind,task,assessment,school_subject,term,revision) NULLS NOT DISTINCT; X (school,enrolment,kind), (school,term,school_subject); C denominator >= 0, numerator >= 0; scored requires denominator > 0 and value 0..1; non-scored value null | Retain immutable calculations, labels/context and supersession chain. Context shape rules below prevent generic untyped result IDs. Year derives from enrolment; no mutable cached mark as source of truth. |
| `result_inputs` / exact source graph and arithmetic contributions | T/I; `result_id -> result_snapshots`, `ordinal`, exactly one of `score_revision_id? -> score_revisions`, `child_result_id? -> result_snapshots` or `unscored_attempt_id? -> learner_attempts`; `moderation_decision_id? -> moderation_decisions`, `weight,raw_value?,normalized_value?,contribution?,disposition,reason?` | U (school,result,ordinal); partial U (school,result,score_revision), (school,result,child_result), (school,result,unscored_attempt); X child_result; C exactly one source, weight 0..1; no cycles; moderation decision composite binds same score revision | Retain all included/excluded/absent inputs and denominators. Unscored attempt is permitted only for absent/exempt/incomplete outcome, same learner/task, with captured status/reason in context_snapshot; never invent a numeric mark. Each excluded input explains why; approved attempt selection is reproducible. Inputs inserted with snapshot in one transaction. |
| `moderation_evidence_refs` / exact relational manifest of reviewed evidence | T/I; `moderation_decision_id -> moderation_decisions`, `evidence_id -> evidence_items`, `asset_id -> file_assets`, `evidence_hash,asset_checksum` | U (school,moderation_decision,evidence); X (school,evidence); composite evidence FK binds asset; validate evidence belongs to reviewed task/attempt or authorized assessment-wide brief | Retain immutable references. Insert with decision and freeze evidence content/context; zero rows is an explicit empty manifest only when policy permits no evidence. Result inputs reach exact retained evidence through the pinned moderation decision. |
| `result_finalizations` / approval seal for one snapshot | T/I; `result_id -> result_snapshots`, `finalized_by_actor_id -> audit_actors`, `finalized_at,content_hash,reason,command_key` | U (school,result), (school,command_key); X (school,finalized_at) | Retain immutable seal; unsealed snapshots are internal candidates. Finalization validates complete approved source graph and separation rules. |
| `result_publications` / release or withdrawal event | T/I; `finalization_id -> result_finalizations`, `audience` (staff/learner/guardian), `action` (publish/withdraw), `sequence,published_by_actor_id -> audit_actors`, `effective_at,reason,supersedes_event_id? -> result_publications` | U (school,finalization,audience,sequence); X (school,finalization,audience,effective_at); self-FK binds same finalization/audience; state machine prevents invalid release/withdrawal | Retain each release/withdrawal; most recent effective event determines visibility. Learner/guardian audience remains disabled until policy approved. A correction needs a new result/seal/release. |
| `report_runs` / generated report/export job and provenance | T/M; `report_type` (learner/subject/class/teacher_assessment/completion/evidence/finalized_result), `purpose` (internal/official), `academic_year_id -> academic_years`, `filters` validated jsonb, `audience,requested_by_actor_id -> audit_actors`, `template_version,status` (queued/running/ready/failed), `asset_id? -> file_assets`, `generated_at?,source_hash?`, `request_key` | U (school,request_key); X (school,requested_by_actor,created_at), (school,status); C ready requires generation timestamp/hash; official ready requires asset | Retain provenance; freeze ready manifest. Internal completion/evidence views may use workflow metadata but must label draft marks and cannot masquerade as official results. |
| `report_result_refs` / relational report source manifest | T/I; `report_run_id -> report_runs`, `finalization_id -> result_finalizations`, `publication_event_id? -> result_publications` | U (school,report_run,finalization); X (school,finalization); publication FK composite binds same finalization | Retain; official external output requires active publication for audience and each learner; download rechecks current visibility even for previously generated PDF. |

Result shape constraints: `task` requires task, assessment and school_subject; `assessment` requires assessment and school_subject, task null; `subject_term` requires subject and term, task/assessment null; `subject_year` and `cumulative` require subject with task/assessment/term null; `term_total` requires term and no subject/task/assessment; `year_total` has none of those context IDs. Task/assessment term follows parent, allowing year-scoped parents. Composite FKs and locked validation ensure enrolment year, term, subject, policy component and academic context agree. A cumulative result belongs to the destination year's enrolment and may reference finalized results from earlier enrolments of the **same school learner** only. Transfers between schools do not silently cross tenant boundaries.

### 3.6 SBA, evidence, reusable storage and current collaboration features

| Table / purpose | Scope / lifecycle; columns and FKs | U / X / C | D / relationships and history |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file_assets` / secure R2 metadata, never file bytes | T/M with immutable ready object metadata; `storage_environment,bucket_alias,object_key,original_name,media_type,byte_size,checksum_sha256?,etag?,uploader_actor_id -> audit_actors`, `state` (pending/quarantined/ready/rejected/delete_pending/deleted), `scan_status,uploaded_at?,retention_until?,legal_hold` | Global U (storage_environment,bucket_alias,object_key); X (school,state,created_at); C byte_size >= 0; ready requires verified metadata and passed applicable scan policy | Retain referenced assets and tombstone metadata; replace content with new asset, never overwrite a referenced key. Bucket alias maps to server config; no secrets, stored signed URLs or public URL authorization. |
| `evidence_items` / educational evidence linked to real context | T/M until submitted/reviewed then frozen; `asset_id -> file_assets`, `assessment_id? -> assessments`, `task_id? -> assessment_tasks`, `attempt_id? -> learner_attempts`, `learner_id? -> learners`, `origin` (teacher/learner), `category` (photo/video/audio/document/other_approved), `caption?,captured_at?,supersedes_id? -> evidence_items`, `withdrawn_at?,withdrawal_reason?` | U (school,asset,assessment,task,attempt,learner) NULLS NOT DISTINCT; X (school,attempt), (school,learner), (school,assessment); C at least assessment or learner present; attempt requires task/assessment/learner; task requires assessment | Retain evidence referenced by review/finalization. Context chain must agree in transaction; standalone learner portfolio evidence allows no assessment. Teacher briefs may have assessment/task and no learner. Uploader identity is distinct from evidence subject. Withdrawal preserves historical link and prevents unauthorized exposure. |
| `folders` / staff and media organization | T/M; `parent_id? -> folders`, `owner_membership_id -> school_memberships`, `section` (staff/media), `name,description?,visibility` (private/staff) | U (school,parent,section,owner,name) NULLS NOT DISTINCT; X (school,section,parent); parent composite FK binds section/owner; reject cycles; child cannot broaden parent visibility | Archive; referenced assets are not deleted with folder. Preserve hierarchy; school membership alone is not access to private resources. |
| `folder_assets` / reusable placement of asset in folder | T/M; `folder_id -> folders`, `asset_id -> file_assets`, `display_name` | U (school,folder,asset); X (school,asset) | Archive link; remove unreferenced draft link with audit. Folder deletion never deletes shared object. Learner evidence cannot be linked to broad staff/media folders without explicit disclosure authorization. |
| `announcements` / secured noticeboard | T/M; `owner_membership_id -> school_memberships`, `title,content,category,visibility` (private/staff), `published_at?` | X (school,visibility,published_at), (school,owner,created_at); U only inherited PK/context; C nonblank title/content | Archive and audit revisions; initial private behavior can preserve current user-scoped notices; staff-wide publication only by authorized admin. |
| `events` / secured calendar | T/M; `owner_membership_id -> school_memberships`, `title,description?,starts_at,ends_at?,location?,visibility` (private/staff), `color?` | X (school,starts_at), (school,owner,starts_at); U only inherited; C end >= start, optional color validated hex | Archive; retain audit. Optional color is proposed capability, not a claim that current schema has the orphan migration column. |
| `storage_jobs` / durable upload reconciliation and deletion outbox | T/M; `asset_id -> file_assets`, `operation` (verify_upload/scan/delete), `idempotency_key,state,attempt_count,next_attempt_at,lease_until?,completed_at?,safe_error_code?` | U (school,idempotency_key); X (state,next_attempt_at); C attempt_count >= 0; completed state requires completed_at | Retain completion/error audit per operations retention; purge processed jobs only under approved policy. DB transaction schedules work; R2 calls happen outside transaction and are retried safely. |
| `audit_events` / append-only domain/security history | Special I; UUID id; `school_id? -> schools`, `actor_id -> audit_actors`, `membership_id? -> school_memberships`, `event_type,resource_type,resource_id?,command_id,sequence,occurred_at,reason?,safe_changes` jsonb, `origin` (native/legacy_import) | U (command_id,sequence); X (school,occurred_at), (actor,occurred_at), (school,resource_type,resource_id); C membership implies school; composite membership FK; school required for business events, null only platform/auth events | Retain append-only. Resource ID intentionally has no polymorphic FK so deletion attempts/legacy events remain recordable; audit references never grant resource access. No tokens, passwords, signed URLs, evidence bytes or unrestricted request bodies. |

Portfolio is a view of learner-linked evidence, not a duplicate file table. Projects, practicals, written tests and portfolios use assessment types/tasks; photos, video, audio and documents are assets/evidence, not assessment-specific blob tables. Teacher evidence includes instructions, demonstrations and observations; learner evidence always identifies the correct learner/attempt independently of who uploaded it.

## A. Entity relationship overview

```text

     |                  |1                  |1
     |                  +---* membership_roles *---1 roles
     |                  +---0..1 staff_profiles

                    +---* platform_role_assignments --- roles

                    +---* class_groups *---1 grades
```

`1---*` means one-to-many; optional links are explicitly marked. Tenant composite FKs apply throughout even where the ERD omits school edges.

## B. Core workflow

1. Authorized platform setup creates school, timezone and initial School Admin membership/role. Create staff through verified Better Auth identity linkage; no school access follows from sign-up alone.
2. Admin creates year/terms, adopts grades and catalogue subjects, creates class/stream groups and offerings. Admit learners, create annual enrolments and dated class/subject placements. Learner logins are unnecessary for staff-led assessment.
3. Admin assigns staff to offerings and reviewers to assessments. Staff without teaching allocation cannot mark simply because they hold Teacher role.
4. Admin selects an approved policy version, creates assessment/tasks and frozen rubric versions, validates weights, then opens and populates the eligible roster. Teachers initially administer admin-created assessments.
5. Create learner task attempts, capture submissions and evidence through authorized pending assets; validate and scan before making assets available. Teacher-uploaded learner evidence retains both uploader and learner identities.
6. Assigned teacher submits a full score revision and criterion rows atomically, then submits for moderation. Incomplete evidence or invalid rubric marks prevents readiness.
7. Assigned independent moderator reviews the exact score/evidence revision and approves or returns it. Returned work produces a fresh score revision and review.
8. School Admin finalizes validated calculations, pinning source revisions, policy, evidence hashes and calculator version. Subject, term, annual and any future cumulative results derive from sealed child outcomes.
9. Authorized School Admin publishes exact sealed versions to approved audiences. Reports reference those versions, not live mutable marks. Corrections create superseding outcomes, explicitly withdraw/release as necessary and preserve the old record.

## C. Authorization matrix

All permissions below require server session, active membership, applicable unexpired role, target school and object/state checks. Initial scope is School Admin and Teacher; other roles describe the proposed boundary, not enabled features.

| Role | Read | Create | Update | Finalize | Publish |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super Admin | Platform school status and platform audit; no default learner/evidence access | Schools and controlled initial admin grants | School operational status/platform grants | No implicit academic authority | No implicit academic authority |
| School Admin | School academic/staff records and scoped evidence; restricted credentials excluded | Academic structure, learners, assignments, assessments, approved policy drafts, notices, reports | School drafts/config; logged score correction workflow only; may moderate with explicit reviewer assignment and independence | Yes, after required independent moderation and completeness checks; cannot silently replace scores | Yes, sealed versions to approved audiences; withdrawal audited |
| Teacher | Assigned offerings, roster/tasks, necessary learner evidence/results | Attempts, permitted evidence, complete score revisions and internal reports for assignments | Own permitted draft submissions; returned scores through a new revision | No; submit for moderation | No |
| Moderator | Only allocated assessment score/evidence scope | Moderation decisions | Return/reject by new decision; no direct mark overwrite | No by role alone | No |
| Learner (future) | Own released results and explicitly visible own tasks/evidence | Own draft attempt/evidence if enabled | Own unsubmitted draft only | No | No |
| Parent/Guardian (future) | Only approved linked learner publications | None initially | None initially | No | No |

Super Admin school support requires a separately approved explicit temporary school membership/role, purpose and audit; no unrestricted tenant bypass. Moderator independence compares stable actors, so assigning both Teacher and Moderator roles does not permit self-review. Proposed finalizer must not be the source assessor; whether moderator and finalizer must also differ is an open decision. Schools without an independent reviewer remain blocked from finalization rather than bypassing review. Teacher assessment creation stays disabled as specified in the governing initial workflow.

Learner login mapping cannot be self-claimed. Guardian access is deferred: a verified, consented, revocable relationship model must be designed before enabling it; no unimplemented generic guardian table is implied here.

Authorization is repeated on every action, query, download, presign, upload completion, report job and background job. Derive school from authorized membership, never trust a caller-supplied school/learner ID. Bind IDs through tenant FKs **and** academic context joins. Check current assignment and historical cohort eligibility separately. Reject cross-tenant IDs, mismatched offerings, inactive memberships, expired assignments, unauthorized transitions and stale row versions. Batch operations authorize each item. Lists/counts/search/dashboard queries must use the same scope. Use controlled not-found/forbidden responses and minimal DTOs.

Asset access requires an authorized attachment context, not just an asset ID or ownership of the upload. Linking existing assets requires authority to disclose the underlying content to the new audience; linking learner evidence to a wide staff folder cannot enlarge access accidentally. Never return object keys to ordinary lists. Issue short-lived signed URLs only after reauthorization, or proxy bytes where immediate revocation matters; already issued URLs remain usable until expiry, which must be reflected in the release policy.

## D. Assessment data flow and reproducible calculations

1. Resolve frozen task, rubric and policy; identify roster/subject enrolment and the selected learner attempt. Absence, missing work, exemption and numeric zero are distinct outcomes.
2. Direct mode records one direct mark. Rubric mode records each criterion with optional matching level. For criterion i, normalized mark is `points_i / max_points_i`; task normalized mark is `sum(criterion_weight_i * normalized_i)`. Task points are that fraction times task maximum. Do not also add direct points.
3. For assessment tasks j, assessment fraction is `sum(task_weight_j * task_fraction_j)`, subject to explicit missing/exempt rules. Do not silently renormalize weights when an input is missing. Denominators, excluded inputs, reason codes and selected attempts are stored in result_inputs/context snapshots.
4. Moderator reviews an exact score revision and evidence manifest. Persist moderation_evidence_refs with the decision, not only an irreversible hash with no list of referenced evidence. A revised mark or evidence set invalidates readiness based on the old review; new approval is required. Store returned and rejected decisions as well as approvals. Required absence/exemption approvals are recorded as authorized audited attempt transitions and captured in the unscored snapshot; they do not fabricate a score revision.
5. Build result snapshot and input rows in one locked transaction. A task input points to a score revision plus matching approval; assessment inputs point to task snapshots; subject-term inputs point to assessment snapshots; subject-year inputs point to subject-term or approved year-scoped assessment snapshots. Term/year totals reference the appropriate subject children. Child graph must be acyclic and at the policy-prescribed level; reject duplicate source inclusion.
6. Finalization seals only complete approved input graphs. For aggregates, each counted child must already have a finalization seal. Store exact decimal numerator/denominator, unrounded intermediate fractions, applied weight, final rounded output/rule, policy/component version, calculator version, input/evidence hash and context labels. Apply rounding only at configured stages; do not recompute historical outcomes using a newer engine.
7. Publication references the finalization, not an arbitrary draft result. Reports select only authorized seals and, for learner/guardian output, active publication events. Ready files are reauthorized against all constituent learners/results. A withdrawn child result makes dependent external reports ineligible until an approved replacement release is prepared.

Illustration only, **not KNEC policy**: criterion fractions 8/10 and 6/10 with weights 0.4 and 0.6 produce 0.68. An assessment with that task at weight 0.25 and another task at 0.80 with weight 0.75 produces 0.77. A missing second task produces an incomplete result unless the approved policy explicitly defines another outcome; it is not automatically 0.17, 0.68 or zero. A configured SBA contribution c produces `SBA_fraction * c` in a downstream policy component, with c recorded as an input weight rather than a Grade 10 column.

Concurrency: serialize marking revisions per attempt; lock relevant policy/task/attempt and review state before committing. Finalization locks the candidate graph and compares input hash/version to prevent concurrent score/evidence changes. Command idempotency keys avoid duplicate scores, seals, reports and storage work. Score append + audit, finalization + audit and publication + audit are indivisible DB transactions. Later evidence additions cannot silently change a sealed manifest.

Corrections never reopen an immutable row for editing. A privileged request records reason, new score/review/snapshot chain and supersedes links, then obtains a new seal and publication. Recalculate affected ancestor snapshots explicitly; retain old dependent reports for audit with withdrawn external access. Finalized learner names/context are preserved in restricted snapshots only to the extent approved reporting retention requires.

## E. Grade 10 SBA as configuration

No official 2026 KNEC document was supplied or verified in R4. This design makes **no claim** about official percentages, task counts, deadlines, scoring bands or submission formats. Source verification is a prerequisite, not an invented answer. No external framework research was performed for this repository design task.

Represent Grade 10 as a grades row. Adopt subject eligibility through subject_grades and school_subjects. Each approved assessment_policies version records grade, subject applicability, effective dates, official title/URI/revision/checksum, reviewer and approval. policy_components represents contribution hierarchy, task categories/counts, weights and period assignment. Bounded versioned settings store evidence requirements and templates; instantiate actual assessments/tasks/rubrics as relational definitions. Version pinning prevents future policy changes from changing prior marks.

The same mechanism supports Grades 11 and 12 and cumulative contribution inputs without grade-specific schema or branching business logic. No cross-year cumulative rule is activated until its approved source and learner continuity rules exist.

Official 2026 KNEC confirmation checklist before implementing Grade 10 policy:

- Applicable circular/manual, publication/revision date, effective cohort and any superseding instructions; approved subject/grade codes and pathway applicability.
- Whether and how Grade 10 SBA contributes to later/cumulative certification; exact contribution weights, denominators, aggregation stages and treatment of transferred/repeating learners.
- Required tasks per subject/term/year, task categories, maxima, rubric descriptors/bands and whether task/criterion or total weighting is prescribed.
- Evidence requirements and permitted formats, authenticity/teacher verification, portfolio contents, group-work individual attribution and accommodations.
- Absence, exemption, incomplete work, late submissions, retakes, selected attempt, rounding and rescaling rules.
- Moderation sampling versus full review, independence, approval authority, finalization/correction windows and audit obligations.
- Submission deadlines, official export/report format and identifiers, publication audience and evidence/result retention durations.

Approval rejects incomplete policy metadata, invalid rubric/weight trees or missing outcome rules. Structural approval can consider this generic model independently, but operational SBA remains disabled until approved official configuration and test vectors exist.

## G. Integrity, security and operational verification

**Database integrity:** Require all catalogue FKs and indexes, composite tenant/context keys, unique admission/academic identities, score revision uniqueness and one finalization per snapshot. Uniqueness with nullable context uses NULLS NOT DISTINCT or explicit partial indexes. Do not use nullable school IDs in tenant tables. Result/policy trees and folder hierarchy require cycle checks. Temporal placements/assignments require overlap prevention under locking or exclusion constraints; any extension needed for exclusion constraints must be separately approved.

**Transactions and privileges:** School bootstrap creates institution/membership/admin role/audit atomically; enrolment changes lock learner/year and placement ranges; publishing configuration validates complete rubric/weight trees and freezes definitions; score writes and criterion completeness validate together; moderation locks reviewed revision and evidence manifest; result finalization seals a consistent graph; publication checks current seal/authority; asset link changes and storage jobs commit together. Use optimistic row_version for ordinary drafts and serialization/row locks for uniqueness/state transitions. Retry conflicts with idempotency, never blind overwrite.

Future application DB role should lack unrestricted UPDATE/DELETE on immutable scoring/audit/seal tables; use restricted domain paths/triggers for guarded transitions. Immutability also prohibits adding child criterion marks, result inputs, review evidence or report manifest rows after their parent transaction has completed: construct the complete unit atomically and enforce closed-parent insertion guards. Tenant query scoping is mandatory. RLS is recommended defense in depth only after testing transaction-local tenant/actor context with the actual pooled connection model and non-owner application role. RLS does not replace assignment/evidence/state checks. No RLS or privileges are changed here.

**Timestamp policy:** New domain times use UTC timestamptz, dates use date, display uses school timezone. Academic dates are calendar dates, due/publication moments are instants. Database-generated event times provide consistency; preserve captured_at separately from upload time. Do not silently change Better Auth timestamp types. Clock ordering alone is not concurrency control; use revisions and sequences.

**Retention:** Archive schools, memberships, staff, learners, curricula and academic structures once referenced. Retain immutable assessment definitions, revisions, evidence manifests, moderation, result inputs, seals and publication history. Auth expiry and operational-job cleanup have separate policies. Evidence purge requires no remaining protected links, elapsed approved retention, no legal hold, explicit authorization and durable deletion job; retain tombstone/checksum/provenance where approved. User deactivation must not cascade into results. No fixed child-data retention duration is asserted without policy review.

**Storage consistency:** Reserve an asset and upload intent before issuing an authorized upload. A completion job verifies actual object size/type/checksum, applies scan policy and marks ready only after success. Failed/expired upload intents are reconciled; no silent exception suppression. Delete workers recheck references/holds under lock, prevent new links while delete_pending, perform idempotent R2 deletion outside the transaction and record completion/failure. Uploaders cannot choose arbitrary existing object keys. Credentials stay in server configuration; bytes remain in R2. Approved access through one context never implies permission to disclose another linked context.

**Required implementation verification (not executed in R4):** Foundation fixtures need two schools, multiple teachers, reviewers, active/inactive memberships and enrolled/unenrolled learners. Cover cross-school composite FK failures, same-school wrong-offering links, admission reuse, class-transfer overlap, inactive assignments, spoofed learner mappings, rubric mismatch/maximums, missing versus zero, exempt denominators, retakes, weight totals, source graph cycles, self-moderation across roles, concurrent mark/finalize conflicts, idempotent retry, immutable seals, publication withdrawal, cached report authorization, shared-asset disclosure and storage failure recovery. Replay Grade 10/11/12 scenarios through the same model, plus separately approved official policy test vectors. Verify auth login/session/logout/invalid-session behavior and current portfolio/media/notice/calendar/dashboard functionality.

Repository scripts currently expose lint but no test/typecheck script; governing docs record missing test/lint setup. That tooling must be established during an authorized implementation phase. R4 verification is document coverage, relationship consistency and change-scope review; no build/typecheck/lint was run because this document changes no executable behavior and generated build artifacts are outside scope.

## H. Open decisions and implementation entry conditions

These remain open; recommendations above are concrete defaults for review, not evidence of owner approval.

| ID | Decision / evidence needed | Required timing |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Owner review/approval of this relational model, naming, data types, retention/deletion defaults and staged table delivery; explicit separate R5 authorization | Before schema/migration creation |
| D2 | Confirm public Better Auth adapter contract/bootstrap, provider ownership of neon_auth and exact Neon project/branch/environment; resolve existing-empty-table baseline and name collisions | Before R5 artifacts are finalized; all target facts rechecked before R6 execution |
| D3 | Approve one membership per user-school with optional multi-school users, school onboarding, role grant/revocation and platform support policy | Before identity schema implementation |
| D4 | Approve single grade per learner-year, readmission numbering, dated class transfers, class-based offerings; decide whether elective cross-class groups or midyear grade changes are required now | Before academic schema implementation; these may change table shapes |
| D5 | Verify official 2026 KNEC sources and all Section E details; decide discrete rubric levels versus required bands, group tasks/individual marks and cumulative transfer handling | Before assessment policy/schema implementation where structural consequences exist; before any operational SBA configuration |
| D6 | Approve moderation coverage/sampling, finalizer independence, correction authority, teacher creation policy (default disabled), and publication audiences | Before assessment workflow implementation |
| D7 | Confirm R2 bucket/environment isolation, legacy-object inventory/retention plan, permitted formats/sizes, scanning, privacy/consent, retention/holds and disclosure policy | Before storage/evidence implementation or metadata disposal/cutover |
| D8 | Decide learner self-service and guardian access release scope; default both disabled. If enabled, design verified guardian linkage and access revocation separately | Before enabling self-service; no implicit guardian schema approval |
| D9 | Approve report templates, external export requirements/identifiers, internal draft labeling and immediate versus expiry-bounded download revocation | Before reporting implementation; resolve mandated structural identifiers before related schema slice |
| D10 | Approve fresh migration history/recovery approach, RLS/DB role enforcement strategy, test runner/lint/CI setup and isolated fixture environment | Before R5 implementation plan is accepted; execution remains Gate R6 |

R4 design completion does not imply that these decisions have been resolved. To begin **any schema implementation**, obtain D1 and a scoped R5 request; resolve D2, D3, D4 and D10 for foundation work, and either resolve D5–D9 for the selected slice or explicitly exclude/defer those dependent capabilities in the approved implementation scope. Full-model implementation requires all applicable structural decisions above resolved. Migration execution, auth test writes, application cutover and disposal remain separate gates in the rebuild plan.

## R4 verification and final status

The design covers all nine requested domains, a per-table contract with inherited explicit defaults, ASCII ERD, school workflow, role matrix, auditable scoring/publication, Grade 10 configuration uncertainties, current-functionality mapping, database integrity and implementation prerequisites. R3's zero-row versus zero-table distinction is preserved. No database/R2 connection or mutation, migration creation, source/auth/environment edit, UI change or R5 work was performed.

**R4 STATUS: PASS** — the design deliverable is complete and ready for review. This is not schema approval or implementation readiness. Exactly what remains before implementation is the scoped approval and decision checklist D1–D10 above; no further phase is started by this status.
